titel: Colleen Lamar:From Diagnosis to Hope: How One Mother's Journey Helped Change Autism Education

einzeiler: A mother shares how raising autistic sons led her to build supportive education systems.
kurzfassung: Colleen Lamar shares her journey of raising autistic sons and navigating early diagnoses without clear guidance. She explains how moving to Germany provided a radically different, positive perspective on autism compared to the US. Her advocacy culminated in co-founding a specialized center at a Texas school and supporting her son's path to a university program.
stichpunkte: Initial autism diagnoses for both sons brought intense behavioral challenges and a complete lack of a roadmap from medical professionals.
Living in Germany for a year shifted the family's perspective, as the local culture viewed late-talking, bright children as a blessing rather than a disability.
After returning to the US, Lamar resisted premature special education placement and educated herself on educational rights.
The family faced thousands of dollars in monthly out-of-pocket costs for classroom therapy before winning an appeal against their insurance provider.
Lamar helped establish the Jeremiah Center in Texas to give neurodivergent students access to top-tier private education and family support.
Her son eventually gained admission to a specialized higher education support program at Vanderbilt University, achieving independence and work experience.

clips.hook: The stark contrast between American and European views on autism
clips.text: Returning from a supportive year abroad meant immediately diving back into the exhausting American process of seeking out various therapists and fighting school systems.

clips.hook: Standing up to a school district by citing legal rights
clips.text: Educating oneself on special education laws and disability acts allowed a parent to successfully challenge a school's decisions regarding their child's placement.

clips.hook: Paying thousands a month out of pocket for classroom therapy
clips.text: A family found themselves footing an enormous monthly bill for classroom therapy support while struggling to understand complex insurance mandates.

clips.hook: A sudden meltdown during a university admissions interview
clips.text: A prospective college student managed a virtual interview for an inclusive higher education program for three quarters of an hour before becoming completely overwhelmed and shutting down.

clips.hook: Mastering city navigation and independence through technology
clips.text: Moving to a college campus in a bustling city taught a young adult how to independently navigate daily routines and travel using mapping applications.

Show Notes:
What happens when a parent refuses to accept that "this is just the way it is"? In this inspiring episode of Why Not Me? Embracing Autism and Mental Health Worldwide, host Tony Mantor welcomes autism advocate Colleen Lamar, whose personal journey as the mother of two autistic sons led to the creation of opportunities that continue to impact countless families.
Colleen shares the emotional story of her sons' diagnoses, the challenges of navigating therapy, education, insurance battles, and public schools, and how a year living in Germany completely changed her perspective on autism. She explains how that experience inspired her determination to advocate for her children and eventually help establish the Jeremiah Center, an innovative educational program that provides neurodivergent students with the opportunity to thrive in a supportive private school environment.
The conversation also explores sibling relationships, faith, advocacy, independent living, the importance of community, and the remarkable success of Vanderbilt University's Next Steps program in helping autistic young adults prepare for meaningful employment and independent lives.
Whether you're a parent, educator, clinician, advocate, or someone seeking a better understanding of autism, this episode offers hope, practical insights, and a powerful reminder that one family's determination can create lasting change for many others.
In this episode you'll hear:
The emotional reality of receiving an autism diagnosis
Why perspective can completely change the autism journey
Lessons learned from living in Germany
Navigating therapies, insurance, and special education
The story behind the Jeremiah Center
Why advocacy begins with parents
Supporting neurotypical siblings
The importance of inclusive education
Vanderbilt's nationally recognized Next Steps program
Building independence in autistic young adults
Faith, resilience, and finding hope through community
Encouragement for parents just beginning their autism journey
